Preliminary version for the project team. Results may change as the study progresses. English translation under review. If the two versions differ, the Portuguese text prevails.
``` ::: ::: ## Context and objective The Agricultural Census, conducted by the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE), asks producers about their land tenure status. One possible answer is **grantee or settler awaiting a definitive title (2017 Census)**, coded as category 46504 in the IBGE Automatic Retrieval System (SIDRA). The category therefore records a **declared** tenure status. The Census does not ask whether an establishment is part of agrarian reform, and producers who have already received their title may declare themselves owners. Drawing on results from Manuscript 1, this page examines how far the category captures agrarian reform in Mato Grosso (MT). ## Data and sources The analysis compares three sets of records. The first covers establishments in the census category, as published by IBGE, both for family farms and for all establishments (family and non-family farms). The second covers agrarian-reform establishments identified in the Census by IBGE jointly with the National Institute for Colonisation and Agrarian Reform (INCRA), using multiple criteria. The third comes from INCRA's administrative records: the projects in the Agrarian Reform Projects Information System (SIPRA) and the list of beneficiaries from INCRA's Regional Superintendency in Mato Grosso. The cards below show the size of each set of records in the state. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## Coverage of agrarian reform by the category @fig-cobertura summarises the main result of the comparison: category 46504 captures at most 26.8% of the agrarian-reform establishments identified in the Census. ::: {#fig-cobertura fig-cap-location="top"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: Agrarian-reform establishments identified in the Census: upper limit inside the census category and lower limit outside it ::: ::: {.achado} Even if all 11,248 establishments in category 46504 were agrarian-reform establishments, they would account for only **26.8%** of the 42,014 that IBGE and INCRA identified in the 2017 Census. At least 30,766 (73.2%) therefore lie outside the category. ::: In family farming, the category's coverage of INCRA beneficiaries in Mato Grosso is 0.116: 8,834 establishments against 76,247 beneficiaries. **Many titled beneficiaries declare themselves owners**: the owners of 10,479 family farms obtained their land through agrarian-reform titling or licence (2017 Census, table 6774). Added to category 46504, these establishments form the **combined measure**, which covers 23.66% of family farms. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

Source: RESA Project Manuscript 1 (in preparation), note to Table A.15; IBGE data, 2017 Agricultural Census; INCRA, list of agrarian-reform beneficiaries in Mato Grosso (Regional Superintendency SR-13; settlers and titled beneficiaries approved up to 30 September 2017), used only for aggregate counts by municipality, with no personal data; Marques (2021). Figures are transcribed from the manuscript’s final results and have not been recalculated.

``` ::: ::: ## Census and INCRA compared by municipality ::: {#fig-censo-incra fig-cap-location="top"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: Census category and INCRA beneficiaries, by municipality ::: @fig-censo-incra shows that the spatial patterns of the two maps diverge: where INCRA records many beneficiaries, the Census often records few establishments in the category. In all, 41 municipalities have 50 or more beneficiaries per 100 family farms and less than 5% of family farms in the category: 29 in T1, 1 in T2, 10 in T3 and 1 in T5. The opposite pattern, with the category at or above the Mato Grosso mean and fewer than 10 beneficiaries per 100 family farms, occurs in 1 municipality (Tesouro). ## External validation If the category measured agrarian reform, municipalities with more INCRA beneficiaries should have more establishments in the category. However, @tbl-spearman shows that the association is weak and loses significance once spatial autocorrelation (the similarity between neighbouring municipalities) is controlled for with Dutilleul's modified t-test. ::: {#tbl-spearman} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: External validation indicators for the census category, by type (provisional labels) ::: The results by type show distinct patterns. T3 accounts for 36.2% of INCRA beneficiaries in Mato Grosso, but the category's coverage there is only 0.027. Its projects are also older: the mean year of creation is 1993.2, and 55.9% of families are in projects created up to 1995. This makes clear that the "low" tenure in the label refers to the status declared to the Census. In T4, 44.0% of beneficiaries are already titled in SIPRA, the highest proportion of any type, and coverage rises to 0.453 once owners titled through agrarian reform are included. In T2, 32.8% of families are in state projects, while T5 has the fewest beneficiaries per family farm (58.4 per 100). @fig-validacao-pontos shows these associations municipality by municipality. ::: {#fig-validacao-pontos fig-cap-location="top"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: Tenure measures and INCRA beneficiaries, by municipality ::: ## Statistical suppression in the category IBGE suppresses cells that could identify a respondent, marking them with the symbol X. In category 46504, X never appears for the number of **establishments**: 106 municipalities have a value and 35 have – (true zero). For **area**, by contrast, X appears in 52 municipalities, leaving 44,431 ha (11.2% of the category's area in Mato Grosso) suppressed. For **persons employed**, X appears in 50 municipalities. For this reason, the percentage of area in the category, by type, covers only municipalities without X (see the [typology](tipologia.qmd) page for the table of type profiles, which reproduces Table 3 of the manuscript). This website never converts the symbol X to zero. **Juara, the host municipality of the Vale do Arinos settlement project (PA)**, is an example of agrarian reform outside the category. It appears with – (true zero) in category 46504, meaning that the Census recorded no family farms with this status, although the municipality has settlement projects in SIPRA. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

Source: RESA Project Manuscript 1 (in preparation), Table 1; IBGE data, 2017 Agricultural Census; Juara: data from this observatory (2017 Census, table 6878; INCRA/SIPRA, 2025). Figures are transcribed from the manuscript’s final results and have not been recalculated.

``` ::: ::: Census category and SIPRA settlement projects, by municipality ::: ## Concluding remarks The census category measures declared tenure status and captures only part of the agrarian-reform establishments identified in the Census. This is evident both in the state aggregate and in the comparisons by municipality and by type. The combined measure, which includes owners titled through agrarian reform, tracks INCRA records more closely than the category alone. The category's association with these records is weak and loses significance when spatial autocorrelation is taken into account. These results have limitations. Area and persons employed in the category are subject to statistical suppression, and the Census and SIPRA have different reference years. The census category should therefore be interpreted as a measure of declared tenure status, not of agrarian reform. Whenever agrarian reform is the subject of analysis, the category must be compared with administrative records.
